brief: TME compiles five charts from Goldman Sachs' 2027 outlook plus a JPMorgan capex estimate. Goldman projects annualized US AI investment reaching 1.4 trillion dollars by end 2027, an economy wide capex cycle. Since ChatGPT launched, AI has driven 21% of US GDP growth but 62% of earnings growth and 92% of market value growth, so markets have priced in AI more than the economy has. JPMorgan estimates each 100 billion dollars of AI capex adds about 9 dollars to S&P 500 EPS, 2.5% earnings growth, in 2027, or about 18 dollars of EPS upside and 4-5 points of added growth at its midpoint assumption. S&P earnings are now a record share of US GDP, raising how much further that share can expand. Forward P/E and PEG ratios sit near 35 year averages, pushing back on bubble claims despite extreme concentration. Separately, Goldman Prime Brokerage reports hedge fund momentum exposure fell to the 23rd percentile of five years from crowded highs, with momentum volatility elevated versus the index. A two day quant rebound, biggest in almost three years, followed, tied by GS PB to momentum renormalization and recovery in crowded trades, leaving open a recovery or a squeeze.
